findings.title: Installation crashes if integration metadata lacks sender.login
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch accesses integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] unconditionally. build_integration only stores metadata.sender when state has a sender, so older integrations, integrations created before the webhook/state was populated, or any installation whose metadata lacks sender will raise KeyError. The result is a 500 instead of the controlled installation-failure page, blocking legitimate installs/reinstalls. Use safe lookup and fail closed when either authenticated user or sender login is missing.

findings.title: New user validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist
findings.body: When Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to the GitHub user who performed the installation. installation_id is still user supplied (request.GET overrides bound state at line 448) and is later used by build_integration to create/attach the integration. If the Sentry Integration row is missing because of webhook delay, deletion, or legacy data, the security check fails open and an OAuth-authenticated user can continue with an arbitrary installation_id. The flow should require a verified sender/installation association or abort when it cannot verify the installer.

findings.title: Failures while fetching the authenticated GitHub user are unhandled
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch catches only exceptions while parsing the access-token response. get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) can raise network errors, HTTP errors, rate-limit errors, or return an unexpected payload. In those cases the request will 500 rather than rendering the intended github-integration-failed error page. Wrap the token exchange/user-info fetch in exception handling and return error(...) for expected failures.

findings.title: installation_id is inserted into the GitHub API path without validation
findings.body: installation_id comes from user input/pipeline state and is interpolated directly into /app/installations/{installation_id}. If a non-numeric or path-containing value is supplied, it may request unintended GitHub API paths. Validate that installation_id matches GitHub's numeric installation ID format (or otherwise sanitize/quote it) before making the API call.
